newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico concerned about gasoline theft--Pemex chief.
newsitem.headline: Mexico concerned about gasoline theft--Pemex chief.

text.p: Rising petty theft of gasoline is damaging Mexico's pipelines and putting the population at risk, oil monopoly chief Adrian Lajous said on Monday.

"Look, the robberies concern us a lot. The danger of these crimes is not just the loss of property for Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), but the serious part is that this type of action puts the population at risk," he told reporters outside of the presidential residence Los Pinos.
In recent months, there have been an increasing number of thefts involving small pipelines, mostly in isolated rural areas. The incidents involved "not very big" amounts of gasoline, he said.
Earlier this month, an attempted gasoline theft started a blaze at the Tula-Azcapotzalco pipeline, injuring four people in a passing car.
Lajous said the gasoline thieves will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law.
"The Mexican government has taken the decision to act with absolute firmness in this material, and of course Petroleos Mexicanos is setting aside more resources to (prevent such theft)," he said.
